newsitem.title: ITALY: TENNIS-CAPRIATI'S ROME RETURN ENDED AFTER ONE DAY.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-CAPRIATI'S ROME RETURN ENDED AFTER ONE DAY.

text.p: Jennifer Capriati enjoyed only a brief visit to the Italian Open on Tuesday, going out in her first match to compatriot Chanda Rubin in straight sets.
The American was joined by France's Nathalie Tauziat, the 15th seed and first to fall in the tournament. She lost in three sets to Belgium's Dominique Van Roost in the second round.
However France's 10th seed Mary Pierce beat Italian wild card Sandra Cecchini in a 6-1 6-1 rout with the Italian crowd recognising their woman was outclassed.
Capriati gave every impression of fighting herself more than her opponent in her first match at the Foro Italico for four years.
Playing in a gusting wind before a small centre court audience that rarely found the energy or the inclination to cheer, the fallen favourite went out 7-6 6-2.

Capriati, whose last appearance was before the teenage burnout in 1993 that led to her facing charges of drugs possession and shoplifting, could only blame herself for failure against a player ranked one place below her 28th slot.
The 1992 Olympic champion had led the first set 5-2 and seemed in complete control until she squandered three set points with the score at 5-3 and serving at 40-0.
Capriati's concentration deserted her and her fragile confidence seemed to drain away as she hit wide and then double-faulted to bring her opponent back to deuce.
Rubin then levelled to 6-6 in a set with eight service breaks and won the tiebreak 7-1 after Capriati again double-faulted on the first set point.
Rubin then ran up a 5-1 lead in the second set with Capriati double-faulting twice in the second game and then on break point in the fourth as her opponent forged 4-0 ahead.
Capriati broke back in the fifth, but needed seven attempts to get there, before Rubin broke straight back in a love game. Capriati then broke her again to 5-2.
She then double faulted in the final game to give Rubin break point and went out with a return to the net.
"She didn't serve very well," said Rubin. "She made a lot more errors than I thought she would. I don't know how many double faults she had but it was a lot.
Rubin now meets Conchita Martinez of Spain, the third seed, winner here for the past four seasons and one of the most highly-fancied players on the clay courts.
Capriati eventually surfaced for a news conference long after the match was over and was clearly struggling to put a brave face on a demoralising defeat.
"I think that I just really lost my concentration," she said. "I think it was just a bad day for me."
